assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md section 'Epic Grouping (by-repository)' lists two Epics: 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. summary-comment.md confirms: 'TC-9006: trustify-backend -- parent: TC-9006 (Feature), contains Tasks 2-4' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui -- parent: TC-9006 (Feature), contains Tasks 1, 5-10'. Two Epics created, one per repository.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md lists Epic summaries as 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. summary-comment.md and impact-map-comment.md consistently use the same format. Both follow '<feature-key>: <repository-name>'.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md table shows all backend tasks (Tasks 2, 3, 4) assigned to Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and all UI tasks (Tasks 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10) assigned to Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Each task's Repository matches its Epic assignment: Tasks 2-4 have Repository 'trustify-backend', Tasks 1, 5-10 have Repository 'trustify-ui'.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md explicitly states: 'Feature "Incorporates" links (Feature -> Epics): TC-9006 incorporates Epic "TC-9006: trustify-backend"; TC-9006 incorporates Epic "TC-9006: trustify-ui"'. Links are from Feature to Epics only, not to individual Tasks.

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks are numbered 2, 3, 4. Frontend tasks that depend on them are numbered 5, 6, 7, 8. summary-comment.md dependency chain confirms: Task 5 depends on Tasks 2, 3 (API contracts); Tasks 6, 7 depend on Task 5 (hooks); Task 8 depends on Tasks 4, 5, 6. All backend task numbers are lower than their dependent frontend task numbers.

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Task 1 (task-1-create-feature-branch.md) is a bookend task, not a documentation or testing task. It is missing 'Files to Modify', 'Files to Create', and 'Implementation Notes' sections. Task 10 (task-10-merge-feature-branch.md) is also a bookend task missing 'Files to Modify', 'Files to Create', and 'Implementation Notes'. Neither is exempted by the documentation/testing carve-out. Tasks 2-8 all have the required sections. Task 9 (documentation) is exempt and correctly includes Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md states under 'additional_fields for Created Issues': 'Epics will additionally have: parent: {"key": "TC-9006"} (Feature as parent)'. The Epic Grouping section uses the word 'Epic' as the issue type name. summary-comment.md confirms: 'TC-9006: trustify-backend -- parent: TC-9006 (Feature)' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui -- parent: TC-9006 (Feature)'.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 10 task files contain a '## Repository' section with exactly one repository name: Tasks 1, 5-10 specify 'trustify-ui'; Tasks 2-4 specify 'trustify-backend'. No task lists multiple repositories.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 10 task files contain '## Target Branch', '## Description', '## Acceptance Criteria', and '## Test Requirements' sections. Verified in task-1-create-feature-branch.md through task-10-merge-feature-branch.md.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: All 10 tasks have corresponding digest files: task-1-digest.md through task-10-digest.md. Each contains '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-hex-chars>'. Example from task-1-digest.md: 'sha256-md:ae8ea05a3f401a533f3a76e45d66671b1062599d302ca28d86ad07d20f6511ca'. All hashes are exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed with 'sha256-md:'.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: Task files include convention references but use free-form prose instead of the prescribed format. Task 2: 'Per repo conventions: use tower-http caching middleware for the summary endpoint route builder to enable response caching.' Task 3: 'Per repo conventions: return Result<Json<PaginatedResults<ProductRemediation>>, AppError> with .context() error wrapping.' Task 6: 'Per frontend conventions: PascalCase for component names, use PatternFly 5 components exclusively.' None of these include the required 'Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>' rationale format prescribed by convention-applicability-rules.md.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md states: 'priority: {"name": "Major"} (inherited from Feature TC-9006)' under 'additional_fields for Created Issues'. summary-comment.md states: 'Priority: Major (propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks)'. Priority 'Major' is explicitly inherited and propagated.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md states: 'fixVersions: [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}] (inherited from Feature TC-9006; fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults section is configured)'. summary-comment.md states: 'Fix Version: RHTPA 1.5.0 (propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks; fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults section is configured)'. fixVersions are correctly inherited with scope defaulting to 'both'.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists and contains an 'Inherited Field Values' section stating: 'Priority: Major (propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks)' and 'Fix Version: RHTPA 1.5.0 (propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks; fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults section is configured)'. Both inherited fields are documented with propagation details.
